title: sub: p2-execution-plane
creator: codex
subtasks: S1 execution-lease data plane: owner identity (instance id + started_at) + lease record (thread_id -> owner / acquired_at / heartbeat_at / expires_at / state) + acquire / renew / release / expire_scan. WRITE-ONLY: _background_tasks still decides everything, zero outward behaviour change. New module backend/db/execution_leases.py following the workflow_events in-module fallback precedent.

S2 status derivation reads the lease: has_active_task is answered by the lease instead of the in-process registry; /status and /list orphan semantics change from 'no task in this process' to 'lease expired'. Existing tripwires reshaped by design (not deleted): test_orphan_detection, test_workflow_stale, test_runner_phase_sync, plus the integration files that poke _background_tasks.

S3 automatic takeover of expired leases: startup + periodic scan resuming from the checkpoint. Takeover may resume the execution loop but may NOT make a decision for a human -- side-effecting nodes (publish/login/upload) are never re-run automatically; those park in a human-decision state and emit an event. Same rule as P2a-S4b's default-refuse and P0-W4's unknown reconciliation.

S4 move long tasks out of the orchestration process -- EVIDENCE-GATED (ruling 1): if S1-S3 yield no observable evidence of a long task occupying the API process, this degrades to a document + per-call-site classification (facts 9 and 13). Note fact 9: Chrome already runs on the host, so this is about the CDP client session, not about moving Chrome.

S5 docs/execution-plane.md: what the lease guarantees and does not guarantee, the single-process reality vs the topology docs/deployment.md describes, the no-DB semantics (durability: none), the automatic-takeover safety boundary, and the per-call-site classification.
notes:
PLANNING ROUND (feat/p2b-s1-execution-lease, commit b69883e1) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was blank (status planning, subtasks [], placeholder jsonl), so this round produced prd.md: fifteen findings each with file:line, a five-slice plan, red lines, acceptance, and the rulings. THE TICKET'S PREMISE WAS REWRITTEN: Dockerfile:81 runs `uvicorn backend.api.app:app --port 8889` with NO --workers, so production is SINGLE-PROCESS (P0's own verification says so at research/p0-claims-verification.md:24) while docs/deployment.md documents a load-balanced three-replica, four-worker topology -- documented end state, not fact. So 'the API process does not hold the real execution lifecycle' is not a defect happening today; what IS happening is that a deploy kills in-flight work and the orphan is only detected, never taken over. Findings that carry the plan: (1) _background_tasks (api/routes/_runner.py:42) documents its own boundary -- cleared on restart, DB rows left at 'running' are 'restart orphans, detected lazily in /list and /status (no startup scan)'; (2) FOUR pieces of process-local state decide what callers observe (_LAST_HISTORY_WRITE, _active_sync_executions, _background_tasks, _last_status at _runner.py:33-45); (3) derive_status(..., has_active_task=True) (state/machine.py:34, priority 9/10 at :129-135) makes RUNNING vs STALE a question about THIS process -- the same checkpoint read elsewhere is a different status; (4) _is_orphan_running (api/routes/workflow.py:389-399) is 'task is None or task.done()', so 'orphan' means 'this process does not have it'; (5) recovery already exists and is human-triggered (POST /recover/{thread_id} at workflow.py:1623, retry_from_last_success via Command(goto=) at :475-491) -- detection exists, automatic takeover does not; (6) there is NO lease/heartbeat/worker/job-queue anywhere in backend/, so the durable scheduler is built from zero; (7) Chrome ALREADY runs out of process on the HOST (docs/deployment.md:284-407), so moving 'XHS Browser' means the CDP client session, not Chrome; (8) db/pool.py is Postgres-only (SQLite is only the dev checkpointer fallback, graph/builder.py:432,612) and the db/ fallback pattern is inconsistent -- workflow_events.py:62-71 has an in-module _mem_events fallback while db/workflows.py has ZERO is_pool_ready checks (the guard is pushed to callers at _runner._db_upsert:71-74). Dependency check: P0's retry consolidation IS delivered (graph/error_handling.py exhaustive RETRY_POLICIES + get_retry_policy raising KeyError), and its comment assigns the 'unified retry engine' to P1/P2 -- recorded as an explicit non-goal. RULINGS (user, 2026-09-16): (1) S4 is evidence-gated -- S1-S3 first, independent worker only if the evidence demands it, else S4 degrades to doc + call-site classification; (2) when is_pool_ready() is false the lease degrades EXPLICITLY with a single reader answering 'durability: none' -- never a silent downgrade, and never fail-closed (that would kill local dev and the whole test suite). Ruling 3 (adopted by discipline, not escalated): automatic takeover may resume the loop but may never re-run a side-effecting node. Tripwires to reshape by design: test_orphan_detection(4), test_workflow_stale(7), test_recover(11), test_publish_retry(8), test_runner_phase_sync(4) plus test_api_routes / test_sse_eventbus / test_workflow_bug_fixes. S1 DELIVERED (feat/p2b-s1-execution-lease, commit 761c2865, PR #614): backend/db/execution_leases.py (+530) is the lease data plane -- owner identity (host:pid:rand + started_at), a per-row ttl_seconds so every expiry judgement reads the row's own budget, and acquire/renew/release/expire_scan/get_lease/list_leases/start_lease/end_lease/ensure_tables/durability, Postgres-first with an in-module fallback following db/workflow_events.py:62-71 (NOT db/workflows.py, which has zero is_pool_ready guards). Wired in at api/routes/_runner.py:327-336 (start, after the sync/async fork, before the try) and :486-492 (end, in the finally after _background_tasks.pop), both inside contextlib.suppress(Exception) because an observational lease must not become a new failure mode; ensure_tables joins the app lifespan's ensure_coros. WRITE-ONLY: nothing reads the lease yet except expire_scan/is_stale, so no answer this service gives changes. cli/main.py is deliberately untouched -- _run_graph_and_persist is only reachable from api/routes/*. Two real defects the tests forced out: acquire judged the incumbent by the CALLER's ttl (which would make one row alive for one reader and dead for another), and the memory fallback handed out the stored object while Postgres builds a fresh record per row. Gates: 3314 passed / 3 skipped (baseline 3283 + 31 new, one for one) / ruff clean / 509 formatted / mypy 205 clean / tool runtime OK / context-compiler drift within threshold. Mutation self-check: 21 mutants, 21 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor failures, sources restored to baseline hashes.

S2 DELIVERED (feat/p2b-s2-status-reads-the-lease, commit b88897d3, PR #615): status derivation reads the lease. _runner gains process_has_active_task (the process registries; verbatim the old inline expression), _lease_is_held (best-effort -- a broken store answers 'not held', not 'held') and has_active_execution (lease OR this process). Seven sites that feed derive_status plus _is_orphan_running moved to it; the two guards that decide whether to START work (brief-upload, publish-retry) deliberately keep reading this process, because both directions are wrong: a bare lease read starts a second execution when the store fails, and asking 'does anyone hold it' refuses a legitimate resume for up to LEASE_TTL_SECONDS after a restart (the dead owner's lease still looks renewable). Orphan semantics change from 'this process has no task' to 'nobody holds the lease'. Fixed an existing defect found on the way: the inline checks at workflow.py:1079 and :1653 had dropped the _active_sync_executions term -- two answers to one question inside one module. Registered cost: inside the 60-90s post-crash TTL window /recover refuses to recover; that is deliberate, bought with red line 4. Reshaped tripwire (not deleted): test_runner_phase_sync::test_phase_falls_back_to_result_when_snapshot_has_no_phase now expects RUNNING -- the old STALE encoded a defect, since only /start's async_mode branch registers in _background_tasks and the foreground /start branch was therefore invisible to has_active_task, which made the runner write 'stale' about a thread it was itself executing. Gates: 3338 passed / 3 skipped (baseline 3314 + 24, one for one) / ruff clean / 512 formatted / mypy 205 clean / tool runtime OK / context-compiler drift within threshold. Mutation self-check: 20 mutants, 20 killed, 0 survived, sources restored to baseline hashes; the first pass had five survivors (M06/M09/M15/M16/M17), each triaged as a real coverage gap and closed with a reader rather than excused. Declared-only gaps (no behavioural test, same expression as the pinned sites): workflow.py:1353, :1653, :1902 -- two report-only fields and a resume-shape choice. S3 ROUND (feat/p2b-s3-takeover-scan, commit 465b55d0, PR #616) -- the lease now CAUSES behaviour instead of merely being read. Two boundaries carried the slice. (1) RED LINE 4 required the lease to fence its own owner: `_fence_on_lost_lease` watches the heartbeat and lets the way it ENDED be the referee -- cancelled by `end_lease` means this run is finishing normally and must not fence, ending by itself means `renew` answered False so the row belongs to someone else, and then the event is set and the host task cancelled. The `CancelledError` branch re-raises before any status write, because writing `cancelled` there would erase the takeover that just started. (2) RED LINE 2 + RULING 3 required the takeover to restore the execution loop without answering for a person, so ONLY the pending nodes (`state.next`) are classified and never the reachable set -- sufficient because the only edge into `publisher` comes from `publish_gate` and `publish_gate` is itself NEEDS_HUMAN; `test_the_only_way_into_the_publisher_is_a_gate` reads that off `build_graph()`'s edges and branches, so the PREMISE is pinned, not just the code. New files: `backend/graph/takeover_safety.py` (exhaustive registry, 13 SAFE / 10 NEEDS_HUMAN / 1 IRREVERSIBLE, unknown name raises KeyError because a default would answer `safe` for a node nobody classified) and `backend/api/routes/_takeover.py` (the scan: refuse / skip / take over, with `acquire` as the single gate; a refusal still writes a `workflow_events` row of kind `takeover`, so `the scan looked and declined` stays distinguishable from `the scan never saw it`; only the rows `expire_scan` JUST flipped are considered, which is what makes repeated cycles idempotent). REAL DEFECT FIXED ON THE WAY: `_acquire_in_memory` asked `not existing.is_stale(now=now)` while `is_stale` means `held AND expired`, so an expired or released row answered False and the `not` turned that into a REFUSAL of a takeover that `_ACQUIRE_SQL`'s `state <> 'held'` grants -- two backends disagreeing about one question, invisible in S1 because nothing yet took over an expired row. GATES: ruff check passed / ruff format 519 files / mypy 207 files / pytest 3411 passed 3 skipped (baseline 3338 + 73 = 71 across 5 new files + 2 lease pins, matching line by line) / context_compiler OK / tool_runtime OK. MUTATION SELF-CHECK 26 mutations, killed=26 survived=0 timeouts=0 anchor_failures=0 restore=OK; the ONE coverage gap was found by asking the question during design (the lifespan wiring had no test at all) rather than by a surviving mutant. | S4/S5 ROUND (feat/p2b-s4-s5-execution-plane-doc, commit e50ee542, PR #617) -- THE EVIDENCE GATE OF RULING 1 CAME BACK NEGATIVE, so S4 degraded to the contract document as designed and S4+S5 shipped as one slice (the degraded output of S4 and the document S5 owed are the same artifact). Four pieces of evidence: (A) all 34 execution points are created by asyncio.create_task and run on awaits -- the signature of 'occupying the process' is absent, they occupy a thread; (B) the only shape that really occupies a request is the non-default path (workflow.py:822 `if req.async_mode:` / :846 `else:` -> :850 _run_graph_and_persist; the model defaults to async_mode=True at workflow.py:502, in full `async_mode: bool = Field(default=True, description="异步执行模式")`); (C) every long task has a bound that can be read statically -- generic tool net `timeout_s=120.0` at tools/runtime/catalog.py:513, publish `_PUBLISH_SAFETY_NET_S = 900.0` at :92, Ripple `_RIPPLE_SAFETY_NET_S = 3600.0` at :82; (D) there is no real sample on this machine (.xhs/checkpoints.sqlite has 0 rows, .xhs/history/*.json are 21-byte test leftovers), so the 'measured occupancy' tier of evidence is unavailable and is not pretended. DELIVERED docs/execution-plane.md (207 lines): what the lease guarantees and does not guarantee, the single-process reality against the topology docs/deployment.md declares, the no-DB durability semantics, the takeover safety boundary, and the per-call-site classification (34 execution points + 9 wiring points). NEW CONCLUSION, section 7 (not a restatement of S1-S3): the plane's promise covers only _run_graph_and_persist -- the single `start_lease(` call site in the whole repo is _runner.py:418, reached by 12 call sites -- while TWO repair paths write the checkpoint directly and take NO lease: workflow.py:2218 `_run_retry` (ripple-retry) and workflow.py:2947 `_run_publish_retry` (publish-retry). They have no lease row, so expire_scan() never sees them and the takeover scan can never pick them up; _run_retry is not even in the task registry (:2302 creates the task with no _runner._background_tasks[thread_id] = task, against :2991 for publish-retry), so /recover cannot see it either. On restart both are NEITHER MIGRATED NOR TAKEN OVER -- and they are exactly the paths most likely to be invoked when a previous run did not finish. REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: both fixes change behaviour (routing them through the single entry would change phase advancement and event emission timing; giving them their own lease would add a refusal branch and a new failure mode) and the gate did not open. The ranked fix list is at the end of section 7. NEW GATE tests/unit/scripts/test_docs_anchors.py (105 lines / 3 cases) -- the repo's FIRST test that reads docs/ (checked: no precedent existed): the doc's tables are delimited by HTML comment markers, and the test asserts that every published file:line still holds its token (43 anchors), that the marker pairs are balanced, that the row floor is met (43 and 3, EXACT values so that a LOST row trips it -- a failure no per-row check can see, because the lost row is not there to be checked), plus 3 absence rows for the negative facts: Dockerfile has no --workers, workflow.py:2302 does not mention _background_tasks, workflow.py never calls start_lease. MUTATION SELF-CHECK 6/6, survived=0, timeouts=0, restore=OK, covering BOTH directions -- the doc lies (wrong line, wrong token, dropped end marker, dropped row, flipped absence) and the code moves (a real line inserted at the top of execution_leases.py). Two findings from the harness: a dropped end marker is caught ONLY by the marker-balance assertion (the non-greedy regex swallowed both tables, so the row floor never fired -- the two assertions cover different failure surfaces and either alone would leak); and the last mutation is the reason the gate exists at all, since doc-internal consistency is not enough. Hardenings carried from S3: anchor precheck before step 0, per-mutation subprocess with a timeout, restore verified by sha256 where the verifier really writes the bytes back, ORIGINALS at module level (os._exit skips finally), plus a new one -- refuse to start on a dirty tree, so a previous crashed run cannot be read in as 'the original'. GATES: ruff check clean; ruff format --check 520 files (was 519); mypy backend --python-version 3.12 on 207 source files; context-compiler baseline drift within threshold; tool runtime gate OK; pytest 3414 passed / 3 skipped (baseline 3411, +3 = exactly the new file's cases). HONEST RESIDUE: the gate pins what the doc SAYS, not whether it is RIGHT -- section 7's reasoning rests on grep, and that grep is itself an absence row in the gate; the two bypass points have no behavioural tests (out of scope here), so whoever fixes them must bring tests, per the S3 lifespan lesson that mutation cannot report on what was never tested; 'workflow.py:2302 is unregistered' is established by grep over the three registration write points (:440/:835/:2991), not at runtime; docs/** and tests/unit/scripts/ are CRLF, so new files must be normalised to the directory's convention (normalise first, then verify -- never 'skip if it already looks CRLF'); the README entries are new in this slice -- before it, nothing in the repo indexed docs/execution-plane.md. This slice closes S4 and S5, so the ticket's slice plan is complete (status/completedAt left untouched, as is this repo's convention).
